synopsis: ISO 34502:2022 supplies a scenario-based safety evaluation framework scoped to road vehicles and limited-access highways; it is methodological precedent, not off-road compliance evidence [f448, f449]. Across chapters, the ISO 34501–34505 process and structure are considered transferable to off-road validation, but their content targets Level 3 and higher road automated driving; useful elements include functional, logical and concrete scenarios originating in PEGASUS [f6642, f7182, f6735]. No heavy-machinery equivalent or study by the listed industry bodies applying ISO 34502 to off-road machines was found, so the programme must define its own scenario or hazard taxonomy for the coverage map [f9881, f1698, f9882]. The standards principally support coverage rather than model credibility: they do not address validation against physical data or risk scaling, establish no physical-to-virtual testing ratio, and do not demonstrate validity for the listed off-road environments and machine conditions [f7693, f8120, f8119, f7694, f7696]. TÜV SÜD nevertheless summarizes European automated-driving regulation and ISO 34502 as requiring the virtual platform itself to be shown fit for purpose, making scenario coverage alone insufficient [f1283, f8120].

Missing physical-data validation clarifies what scenario standards alone cannot establish about platform fitness.
